               <span class="num"><span>(72)</span></span><span>To ensure a high level of cybersecurity, it is necessary to prevent </span><span>high-risk suppliers</span><span>, as identified in accordance with [the proposal for a revised Cybersecurity Act]</span><span> </span><span>from</span><span> supply</span><span>ing critical components</span><span> to bidders of renewable energy auctions, tenderers of public procurement procedures, and final products supported by government intervention in the scope of this Regulation. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(73)</span></span><span>Furthermore, the cybersecurity provisions of Article 26 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 should not only apply to 30</span><span>%,</span><span> but to all renewable energy auctions</span><span> in light that</span><span> cybersecurity is essential to the stability and integrity of the Union’s energy system as a whole. A gap even in just one element of an energy system’s cybersecurity </span><span>could</span><span> </span><span>endanger the stability of the whole system. </span><span>In addition to the high level of cybersecurity ensured in critical sectors by </span><span>Directive (EU) 2022/2555 </span><span>and in products with digital elements under </span><span>Regulation (EU) 2024/2847</span><span>, </span><span>e</span><span>xtending the scope of the cybersecurity requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 </span><span>to all renewable energy auctions </span><span>should </span><span>further</span><span> reduce the vulnerabilities of the Union’s energy system and contribute to securing energy and economic stability.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(74)</span></span><span>The</span><span> application of the</span><span> requirements on Union origin and cybersecurity for net-zero technologies should complement t</span><span>he</span><span> requirements on sustainability and resilience </span><span>set out</span><span> </span><span>in Regulation (EU) 2024/1735. They should therefore be inserted in </span><span>that </span><span>Regulation </span><span>to</span><span> ensure consistency and simplify implementation by the relevant authorities.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(75)</span></span><span>In line with the measures for public procurement, auctions and public support schemes, this Regulation should also complement Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 with Union origin requirements for Member State support to the construction of nuclear power plants and to the manufacturing of hydrogen electrolysers. To secure long term </span><span>Union</span><span> sovereignty, energy security, and sector resilience, it is essential that the </span><span>new</span><span> nuclear plants, both large scale reactors and small modular reactors, prioritise as much as possible Union sourced technologies and components while maintaining the highest quality standards. </span><span>Such</span><span> strategy will not only boost domestic capabilities but also position the Union as a reliable, competitive player in the global nuclear market.</span><span> However, in order to prevent risks related to technological lock-in, the Union origin requirements for nuclear power plants should only apply to new-builds, excluding refurbishments and lifetime extensions of existing nuclear power plants. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(76)</span></span><span>Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 should therefore be amended accordingly.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(77)</span></span><span>Hydrogen is a crucial energy carrier for the energy transition in many industry applications and is instrumental in driving the transition to cleaner energy systems. To accommodate the emergence of gigawatt scale electrolyser deployments in the </span><span>Union</span><span>, </span><span>it</span><span> is essential</span><span> to have </span><span>a concerted, enhanced support system is essential.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(78)</span></span><span>Where Union origin requirements </span><span>require that a certain number of components should originate in the Union without specifying which </span><span>ones</span><span>, the choice </span><span>should be left to the economic operators</span><span>. </span><span>This ensures sufficient competition among suppliers of the required components and enables economic </span><span>operators to make the most cost-efficient choices while applying the requirements. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(79)</span></span><span>Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 empowers the Commission to adopt delegated acts to establish environmental sustainability labelling requirements for specific product categories and families of construction products, provided that a product is typically chosen by consumers and does not have a different overall environmental performance over its life cycle depending on its installation. </span><span>Such</span><span> strict conditions should be removed in order to enable the Commission to set requirements for the labelling of construction products on the basis of their carbon intensity, </span><span>including</span><span> </span><span>for those products that are not typically sold to end consumers.</span><span> </span><span>Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 should therefore be amended accordingly.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(80)</span></span><span>To the extent that any of the measures envisaged by this Regulation constitute State aid, the provisions concerning such measures are without prejudice to the application of Articles 107 and 108 TFEU.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualConsidrant">
               <span class="num"><span>(81)</span></span><span>Since the objective of this Regulation, namely to support resilient and decarbonised industrial production, cannot be sufficiently achieved by the Member States and can rather, by reason of the scale or effects of the action, be better achieved at Union level, the Union may adopt measures in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in Article 5 of the Treaty on European Union. In accordance with the principle of proportionality as set out in that Article, this Regulation does not go beyond what is necessary in order to achieve that objective,</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Formuledadoption">
               <span>HAVE ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="ChapterTitle">
               <span>CHAPTER I</span><span>
                  <br/>GENERAL PROVISIONS</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>1</span><span> </span>
               <br/>
               <span>S</span><span>ubject matter and s</span><span>cope</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>This Regulation </span><span>aims at improving the functioning of the internal market by establishing a framework </span><span>to support the development</span><span>,</span><span> competitiveness </span><span>and resilience </span><span>of the Union's manufacturing sector, with a focus on </span><span>selected </span><span>strategic sectors, </span><span>while contributing to the Union’s climate objective,</span><span> </span><span>economic security and </span><span>the creation, retention of, and transition into</span><span> high-quality jobs.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>To achieve the general objective referred to in paragraph 1, this Regulation lays down measures aiming to</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>speed-up permit-granting procedures for industrial manufacturing projects, including energy-intensive industry decarbonisation projects; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>create lead market for </span><span>certain products in strategic sectors, </span><span>by laying down </span><span>Union origin requirements, low-carbon requirements, or both, in the context of public procurement, public support schemes; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>set conditions on </span><span>foreign direct investments in emerging strategic sectors; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>designate </span><span>industrial manufacturing acceleration areas</span><span> </span><span>by Member States </span><span>for the purpose</span><span>s</span><span> of boosting industrial activities</span><span>.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>2</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Industrialisation objective</span><span> </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>The Union and Member States shall seek to ensure that by 2035 the manufacturing industry of the Union accounts for at least 20% of the Union’s gross domestic product. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>3</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Definitions</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(1)</span></span><span>‘industrial manufacturing project’ means the construction</span><span>,</span><span> conversion </span><span>or extension </span><span>of an industrial site intended for carrying out an economic activity classified under NACE Code C (Manufacturing)</span><span>, with the exception of NACE Code C12</span><span>; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(2)</span></span><span>‘energy</span><span>-</span><span> intensive industries’ means the industries listed in </span><span>point 1 of </span><span>Annex I;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(3)</span></span><span>‘energy‘energy-intensive industry decarbonisation projects’ means the construction or conversion of the commercial facility of an energy-intensive business as defined in Article 17(1), point (a), of </span><span>Council</span><span> </span><span>Directive 2003/96/EC</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref52" href="#footnote52">52</a>
               </span><span> in the energy</span><span>-</span><span> intensive industries listed in </span><span>point 1 of </span><span>Annex I </span><span>to</span><span> </span><span>this Regulation that reduce emission rates of CO2 -eq of industrial processes significantly and permanently to an extent which is technically feasible;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(4)</span></span><span>‘permit-granting procedure’ means a process that covers all relevant permits to build, expand, convert and operate industrial manufacturing projects, including building, chemical and grid connection permits</span><span> as defined in </span><span>Article 1 of</span><span> </span><span>[</span><span>the </span><span>Proposal for a </span><span>Directive </span><span>amending Directives (EU) 2018/2001, (EU) 2019/944, (EU) 2024/1788 as regards acceleration of permit-granting procedures</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref53" href="#footnote53">53</a>
               </span><span>]</span><span>, and environmental assessments and authorisations where required, and encompassing all applications and procedures from the acknowledgement that the application is complete to the notification of the comprehensive decision on the outcome of the procedure;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(5)</span></span><span>‘comprehensive decision’ means the decision or set of decisions taken by a Member State authority or authorities, that determines whether or not a project promoter is authorised to build, expand, convert and operate an </span><span>industrial manufacturing</span><span> project;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(6)</span></span><span>‘contract’ means public </span><span>contract</span><span> as defined in Article 2(1), point (5), of Directive 2014/24/EU</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref54" href="#footnote54">54</a>
               </span><span>, supply, works and service contracts as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Directive 2014/25/EU</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref55" href="#footnote55">55</a>
               </span><span>, and concessions as defined in Article 5, point (1), of Directive 2014/23/EU;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(7)</span></span><span>‘contracting authority’ means a contracting authority as defined in Article 6 of Directive 2014/23/EU, Article 2(1), point (1), of Directive 2014/24/EU and Article 3 of Directive 2014/25/EU;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(8)</span></span><span>‘contracting entity’ means a contracting entity as defined in Article 7 of Directive 2014/23/EU and Article 4 of Directive 2014/25/EU; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(9)</span></span><span>‘economic operator’ means the manufacturer, the authorised representative, the importer, the distributor, the dealer and the fulfilment service provider</span><span> and,</span><span> for the purposes of public procurement procedures, </span><span>it</span><span> means economic operator as set out in Article 5</span><span>, point </span><span>(2)</span><span>, of</span><span> Directive 2014/23/EU, Article 2(1)</span><span>, point </span><span>(10)</span><span>, of</span><span> Directive 2014/24/EU and Article 2</span><span>, point </span><span>(6)</span><span>, of</span><span> Directive 2014/25/EU;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(10)</span></span><span>‘public procurement procedure’ means either of the following:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>a procedure for the award of works or a service concession covered by Directive 2014/23/EU; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>any type of award procedure covered by Directive 2014/24/EU for the conclusion of a public contract or Directive 2014/25/EU for the conclusion of a supply, works and service contract;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(11)</span></span><span>‘</span><span>greenhouse</span><span> gas </span><span>intensity’ means emissions (measured in tCO2eq) released during the production of industrial products </span><span>referred to in Article </span><span>10</span><span>(2); </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(12)</span></span><span>‘manufacturer’ means any natural or legal person that manufactures a product or that has a product designed or manufactured, and markets that product under their name or trademark;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(13)</span></span><span>‘system boundary’ means the group of chemical or physical processes included in the calculation of the greenhouse gas intensity of products;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(14)</span></span><span>‘precursor’ means any input material into a production process that is part of the system boundaries.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(15)</span></span><span>‘chemical industry’ means activities classified under NACE Rev. 2, Code C20 (Manufacture of chemicals and chemical products), carried out by manufacturers established in the Union;</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(16)</span></span><span>‘sustainable carbon sources’ means biomass that complies with the sustainability criteria laid down in Article 29 of Directive (EU) 2018/2001, waste and carbon from capturing carbon dioxide emissions. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(17)</span></span><span>‘substance’ means substance as defined in Article 2, point (7), of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(18)</span></span><span>‘mixture’ means a mixture as defined in Article 2, point (8), of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(19)</span></span><span>‘made available on the market’ means </span><span>any supply of a product for distribution, consumption or use on the Union market during a commercial activity, whether against payment or free of charge;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(20)</span></span><span>‘fuel cell vehicle’ or ‘FCV’ means a vehicle equipped with a powertrain containing exclusively </span><span>energy converter</span><span>s</span><span> transforming chemical energy (input) into electrical energy (output)</span><span>,</span><span> or vice versa</span><span>,</span><span> </span><span>and electric machines as propulsion energy converters;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(21)</span></span><span>‘motor vehicle’ means any vehicle of categories M and N referred to in Article 4(1), points (a) and (b), of Regulation (EU) 2018/858</span><span> </span><span>of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref56" href="#footnote56">56</a>
               </span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(22)</span></span><span>'off-vehicle charging hybrid electric vehicle' or 'OVC-HEV' means a vehicle equipped with a powertrain containing at least two different categories of propulsion energy converters where one of the propulsion energy converters is an electric machine that can be charged from an external source'</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(23)</span></span><span>‘</span><span>pure</span><span> electric vehicle’ or ‘PEV’ means a vehicle equipped with a powertrain containing exclusively electric machines as propulsion energy converters and exclusively rechargeable electric energy storage systems as propulsion energy storage systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(24)</span></span><span>‘main specific components’ means the main specific components as listed in the Annex to Commission Implementing Regulation 2025/1</span><span>178</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref57" href="#footnote57">57</a>
               </span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(25)</span></span><span>‘vehicle’s traction battery’ means the electric vehicle battery specifically designed to provide electric power for traction as defined in Article 3(14) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref58" href="#footnote58">58</a>
               </span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(26)</span></span><span>‘e-powertrain components’ means power electronics, </span><span>transport propulsion electric motors</span><span> </span><span>and e-axles and their components, rotors and stators</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(27)</span></span><span>‘main electronic systems’ means advanced driver assistance systems (including lidars, radars, sensors, cameras, ECUs and integration platforms), central computing units, wireless access systems, in-vehicle infotainment head units and chassis electronics;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(28)</span></span><span>‘vehicle component’ means any part of a vehicle, including processed material;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(29)</span></span><span>‘assembled’ means the process of the final assembly of the vehicle;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(30)</span></span><span>‘vehicle manufacturer’ means a natural or legal person who is responsible for all aspects of the type-approval of a vehicle, system, component or separate technical unit, or the individual vehicle approval, or the authorisation process for parts and equipment, for ensuring conformity of production and for market surveillance matters regarding that vehicle, system, component, separate technical unit, part and equipment produced, irrespective of whether or not that person is directly involved in all stages of the design and construction of that vehicle, system, component or separate technical unit concerned</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(31)</span></span><span>‘foreign direct investment’ means an investment</span><span>, including greenfield investments,</span><span> into a Union target or a Union asset by </span><span>a foreign investor</span><span> or by the foreign investor’s subsidiary aiming to establish or to maintain lasting and direct links between the foreign investor and the entrepreneur to whom or the undertaking to which the capital is made available</span><span>, or at using an Union asset,</span><span> in order to carry on an economic activity in a Member State, including investments which enable effective participation in the management or control of a company carrying out an economic activity;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(32)</span></span><span>‘foreign investor’ means a natural person of a third country who does not hold the nationality of a Member State or an undertaking of a third country, intending to make or </span><span>having made</span><span> </span><span>a foreign direct investment;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(33)</span></span><span>‘foreign investor’s subsidiary’ means an undertaking </span><span>controlled, directly or indirectly, by a foreign investor regardless of its place of establishment</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(34)</span></span><span>‘Union target’ means an undertaking established under the laws of a Member State;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(35)</span></span><span>‘Union asset’ means an immovable asset used or intended to be used for manufacturing products in the territory of the Union; </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(36)</span></span><span>‘Union worker’ means any natural person who has an employment contract or employment relationship as defined by law, </span><span>a</span><span> collective agreement or practice in force in a Member State and is either a citizen of the Union or a third country national legally residing in a Member State </span><span>with a valid work permit at the moment of recruitment</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(37)</span></span><span>‘</span><span>portfolio</span><span> investment’ means</span><span> </span><span>the </span><span>acquisition of company securities that are intended purely for financial investment and without any intention to influence the management or control of the company</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(38)</span></span><span>‘turnover’ means the amount derived by an undertaking within the meaning of Article 5(1) of Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref59" href="#footnote59">59</a>
               </span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(39)</span></span><span>‘active material’ means a material which reacts chemically to produce electric energy when the battery cell discharges or to store electric energy when the battery is being charged;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(40)</span></span><span>‘electric vehicle battery’ means </span><span>an electric vehicle battery as defined in Article 3(1), point (14), of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542</span><span> of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref60" href="#footnote60">60</a>
               </span><span>;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(41)</span></span><span>‘supplier’ means a manufacturer established in the Union, the authorised representative of a manufacturer who is not established in the Union, or an importer, who places a product on the Union market;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="ChapterTitle">
               <span>CHAPTER II</span><span>
                  <br/>ENABLING CONDITIONS FOR INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION AND DECARBONISATION</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>4</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Single access points</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Member States </span><span>shall set up a single access point at national level for </span><span>the submission by project promoters of the single application </span><span>for industrial manufacturing projects referred to in Article 5(1). </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The single access points shall</span><span> </span><span>automatically attribute the permit applications to the relevant </span><span>authority, </span><span>inform the applicant about all steps of the permit-granting procedure, the status of the procedure and of the decisions of the relevant authorities, and enable the applicant</span><span> </span><span>to check</span><span> compliance with applicable deadlines. </span><span>To that effect the single access points shall use the European Business Wallets established </span><span>pursuant to [Proposal for a Regulation on the establishment of European Business Wallets].</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Through the use of European Business Wallets, the single access points shall enable:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>interoperability and automated data exchange between competent authorities; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>re-use of data and documents already held by public authorities;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>a high level of cybersecurity, and integrity of information; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>transparency and accountability of the permit-granting procedure.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>When setting up the single </span><span>access points</span><span>, Member States shall, where appropriate, make use of existing Union digital infrastructure, catalogues and building blocks established by Union law. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>5</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Permit-granting procedure</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Member States shall establish a single </span><span>permit-granting procedure based on a single </span><span>application covering all permits required for </span><span>industrial manufacturing</span><span> project</span><span>s.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>Member States shall </span><span>designate a competent authority </span><span>to </span><span>coordinate </span><span>the</span><span> </span><span>permit-granting </span><span>procedure </span><span>referred to in </span><span>paragraph 1 in order to ensure </span><span>the adoption and issu</span><span>e</span><span> of a comprehensive decision</span><span> within the applicable time limit</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>No later than 45 days from the receipt of the application for a permit </span><span>for industrial manufacturing projects</span><span>, the competent authority shall </span><span>either </span><span>acknowledge that the application is complete or request any missing information needed to process the application. </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Where, after the submission of any missing information, the application is still deemed to be incomplete, the competent authority may, within 30 days of the submission of the requested missing information, make a second request for any information still missing. The competent authority shall not request information in areas not covered in the first request for additional information and shall request further information only as necessary to cover the missing information.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>The provisions of this Article shall not apply where rules to streamline the administrative and permit-granting processes are established in other Union legislative acts for specific industrial manufacturing sectors.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>6</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Energy</span><span>-</span><span>intensive industry decarbonisation projects</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>C</span><span>hapter</span><span> II, Section II, of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 shall apply to all energy-intensive industry decarbonisation projects. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>A</span><span>ll energy</span><span>-</span><span>intensive </span><span>industry </span><span>decarbonisation projects shall be considered strategic projects </span><span>contributing to resilience and decarbonisation or resource efficiency</span><span> </span><span>for the purposes</span><span> of [Article 14 of Proposal for a Regulation on speeding-up </span><span>environmental assessment</span><span>]</span><span>. Points 1, 2 and 3 of the Annex in that Regulation shall apply.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="ChapterTitle">
               <span>CHAPTER III</span><span> </span><span>
                  <br/>STRENGTHENING THE UNION’S STRATEGIC INDUSTRIAL VALUE CHAINS</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>7</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Union origin</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>For the purposes of this Chapter, content of Union origin refers to content originating in the Union.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The</span><span> </span><span>origin of products </span><span>and components </span><span>shall be determined in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 8</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Content equivalent to Union origin in public procurement</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>With respect to the Union origin requirements referred to in Article </span><span>11</span><span>, content originating in third countries with which the Union has concluded an agreement establishing a free trade area or a customs union, or that are parties to the Agreement on Government Procurement</span><span>, where relevant obligations of the Union exist under that agreement,</span><span> shall be deemed to be of Union origin</span><span>.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The </span><span>Commission</span><span> </span><span>shall </span><span>adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article </span><span>30</span><span> to exclude, in whole or in part, a third country from the scope of paragraph 1 based on any of the following criteria: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>that third country has failed to provide national treatment related to Union products or entities under the agreements referred to in paragraph 1 in relation to any of the sectors listed in Annex I</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>such exclusion is justified to avoid dependencies or any other developments that may threaten the security of supply in the Union of the products in question;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>such exclusion</span><span> is justified under any other exception under the applicable agreement.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 9</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Content equivalent to Union origin in other forms of public intervention</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>With respect to the Union origin requirements set out in Article 12, content originating in third countries with which the Union has concluded an agreement </span><span>establishing</span><span> a free trade area or a customs union shall be deemed to be of Union origin</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The </span><span>Commission</span><span> </span><span>shall </span><span>adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article </span><span>30</span><span> to exclude, in whole or in part, a third country from the scope of paragraph 1 based on any of the following criteria: </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>that third country has failed to provide national treatment related to Union products or entities under the agreements referred to in paragraph 1 in relation to any of the sectors listed in Annex I;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>such exclusion is justified to avoid dependencies or any other developments that may threaten the security of supply in the Union of the products in question;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>such exclusion is justified under any other exception under the applicable agreement.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>10</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Low-carbon </span><span>products</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>For </span><span>t</span><span>he purposes of this Chapter, a product covered by </span><span>Annex II shall</span><span> be considered low-carbon when it complies with the </span><span>requirements</span><span> set out in delegated acts, as follows:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>f</span><span>or construction products </span><span>referred to</span><span> in </span><span>Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 and </span><span>covered by a harmonised technical specification or a European Technical Assessment</span><span>, the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 5(5) or Article 22(9) of Regulation</span><span> (EU) 2024/3110</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>f</span><span>or </span><span>all</span><span> other products, </span><span>delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, as applicable</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>To support </span><span>the creation of lead markets </span><span>by </span><span>informing investment decisions towards products granted a lower greenhouse gas intensity performance class</span><span>, t</span><span>he Commission is empowered</span><span> </span><span>to adopt delegated acts in accordance with </span><span>Article </span><span>30</span><span> </span><span>in order to supplement </span><span>this Regulation by </span><span>establishing </span><span>voluntary </span><span>classification systems based on the greenhouse gas intensity for products manufactured through activities listed in Annex I of Directive 2003/87/EC (‘industrial products’) when they are placed on the Union market, to the extent that these products are not </span><span>already </span><span>regulated by a Delegated Act under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 or </span><span>included in the working plans adopted in accordance with </span><span>that </span><span>Regulation</span><span>. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Emissions and all other relevant data used for the calculation of the greenhouse gas intensity shall be verified by verifiers accredited under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067 </span><span>of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref61" href="#footnote61">61</a>
               </span><span> or verifiers accredited under the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956, as appropriate. Emissions shall be monitored in accordance with the rules laid down in Chapter III of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 and the data monitoring methods and quality requirements set out in Annex VII to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331. For imported products, emissions may be monitored in accordance with Annex IV to Regulation (EU) 2023/956 and the data monitoring methods and quality requirements established by implementing acts adopted pursuant to Article 7(7), point (a), of Regulation (EU) 2023/956, where it provides for an equivalent dataset. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Such delegated acts shall specify, as appropriate, the following elements:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the </span><span>identification of the product for which a manufacturer may apply for a label on greenhouse gas intensity; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the relevant system boundaries, covering emissions from the industrial manufacturing process, emissions from relevant precursors and emissions from electricity consumption. These emissions are considered independently of whether these emissions occur in the manufacturer’s facility or in other facilities, recognising that certain precursors might be acquired from other installations</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the methodology for the calculation of the greenhouse gas intensity of the product </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>a classification with performance classes;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>complementary rules concerning the governance of the label, including competent entities; and </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>complementary rules</span><span> on accreditation, monitoring and verification,</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>In developing those rules, the Commission shall at least take into account:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the latest applicable product benchmark values as defined under Directive 2003/87/EC;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>data already available under the EU ETS and CBAM;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>new Union rules concerning accounting for emissions, including from electricity consumption, low-carbon fuels and renewable fuels of non-biological origin;</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>emerging low-carbon production technologies, as well as the estimated emissions’ reduction potential of emerging technologies; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>the need to </span><span>incentivise</span><span> </span><span>the uptake of </span><span>recycled materials</span><span> </span><span>in all production routes</span><span>;</span><span> and</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>the alignment with climate neutrality objectives, as laid down in Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref62" href="#footnote62">62</a>
               </span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>11</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Public procurement</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>C</span><span>ontracting authorities and contracting entities shall </span><span>exclude from access </span><span>to </span><span>procurement procedures </span><span>referred </span><span>to in </span><span>Part I of </span><span>Annex II and </span><span>Part I of Annex</span><span> III </span><span>tenders </span><span>submitted by</span><span> </span><span>economic operators</span><span> </span><span>owned or controlled by an entity established in </span><span>third countries</span><span> which have not concluded an international agreement with the Union guaranteeing such access</span><span>.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>For p</span><span>ublic procurement procedures referred to in </span><span>Part I of </span><span>Annex </span><span>I</span><span>I and </span><span>Part I of Annex</span><span> III</span><span>,</span><span> </span><span>contracting authorities and contracting entities shall apply</span><span> </span><span>the</span><span> Union origin requirements</span><span> and</span><span> low-carbon requirements </span><span>laid down therein</span><span> in </span><span>accordance with Articles </span><span>8</span><span> and </span><span>10</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>Contracting authorities and contracting entities </span><span>may decide not to apply </span><span>the requirements set out in Annex</span><span>es</span><span> II and III where any of the following conditions </span><span>are</span><span> fulfilled</span><span>: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the required products or services can only be supplied by one specific economic operator, and no reasonable alternative or substitute exists, and the absence of competition is not the result of an artificial narrowing down of the parameters of the public procurement procedure;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>no suitable tenders or no suitable requests to participate were submitted, including in response to a similar former public procurement procedure launched by the same contracting authority or contracting entity in the two years preceding the start of the planned new procurement procedure;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>their application would require a contracting authority or contracting entity to acquire goods, services or works having disproportionate costs or would result in technical incompatibility in their operation and maintenance. Estimated cost differences exceeding </span><span>25</span><span>%, based on objective and transparent data, may be presumed by contracting authorities and contracting entities to be disproportionate</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Contracting authorities and contracting entities shall require economic operators supplying products or services to submit a self-declaration, or an equivalent document, demonstrating compliance with the requirements set out in this </span><span>Article</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 1</span><span>2</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Other forms of public intervention</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Without prejudice to Articles 107 and 108 TFEU, </span><span>Member States shall design </span><span>public support schemes </span><span>in a way that they contribute to the objective of strengthening the Union’s strategic industrial value chains through </span><span>the Union origin requirements, low-carbon content requirements, or both, laid down in Part II of Annex II</span><span> and Part II of Annex III</span><span>, in accordanc</span><span>e</span><span> with Articles </span><span>9 and 10</span><span> and without prejudice to Article 13</span><span>. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Member States shall apply the requirements referred to in the first subparagraph to public support schemes accounting for at least 45% of the total national budget allocated to the public support schemes covered by Part II of Annex II and accounting for 100% of the total national budget allocated to the public support schemes covered by Part II of Annex III. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>When designing and implementing a public support scheme covered by </span><span>Part II of </span><span>Annex II</span><span> and Part II of Annex III</span><span>, the </span><span>competent </span><span>authority shall assess the </span><span>contribution</span><span> of products and technologies </span><span>to the overall target </span><span>laid down therein on the basis of an open, non-discriminatory and transparent process.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>The competent authority may still implement support schemes that do not meet the requirements laid down in Part II of Annex II and Part II of Annex III, in whole or in part, if the application of such requirements:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>would lead to significant delays due to the unavailability of the required components or final products. Estimated delays in excess of seven months, based on objective, transparent and verifiable data, may be presumed to be significant</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>would incur disproportionate costs. Disproportionate costs shall be presumed to exist where, based on objective, transparent and verifiable data, compliance would increase the cost of the underlying final product or technology by more than 30%. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 13</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Financial support for corporate vehicles </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>For the purposes of Article 4 of the [Proposal for a Regulation of 16 December 2025 on clean corporate vehicles], the ‘made in the European Union’ criterion for providing financial support for the uptake of corporate cars and vans shall comply with the criteria set out in Part II of Annex III to this Regulation. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>This ‘made in the European Union’ criterion shall be considered equivalent to the ‘Union origin’ referred to in Article 7 of this Regulation.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 1</span><span>4</span>
               <br/>
               <span>CO2 emission</span><span> performance standards </span><span>credits</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>For the purposes of Article 5</span><span>(1) and (2)</span><span> of Regulation (EU) 2019/631</span><span> </span><span>[as amended by the Proposal for a Regulation of 16 December 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/631 as regards CO2 emission performance standards for new light duty vehicles and vehicle labelling], </span><span>the</span><span> ‘made in the EU’ </span><span>criterion for </span><span>small zero-emission vehicles </span><span>shall comply with the criteria</span><span> set out in Part </span><span>III</span><span> of Annex III</span><span> to this Regulation</span><span>. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>This ‘made in the EU’ criterion shall be considered equivalent to the ‘Union origin’ referred to in Article 7 of this Regulation.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>For the purposes of Article 5b of Regulation (EU) 2019/631 [as amended by the Proposal for a Regulation of 16 December 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/631 as regards CO2 emission standards for new light duty vehicles and vehicle labelling], ‘low-carbon steel made in the EU’ shall be understood as follows:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>‘low</span><span>-</span><span>carbon’ </span><span>shall comply with the conditions referred to in Article 10(1) of this Regulation; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>‘made in the EU’ </span><span>shall be equivalent to the ‘Union origin’ referred to in Article 7 of this Regulation.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Normal"/>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>1</span><span>5</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Certification of a vehicle’s compliance with Union origin requirements </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>From [OP please insert date: six months after entry into force], when issuing a vehicle’s certificate of conformity in accordance with Articles 36 and 37 of Regulation (EU) 2018/858, for vehicles in compliance with the relevant Union origin requirements laid down in Annex III to this Regulation, manufacturers shall provide an accompanying document certifying the compliance of the vehicle.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 1</span><span>6</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Delegation of powers</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article </span><span>30</span><span> </span><span>to supplement this Regulation by laying down Union-level demand-side measures for products from the chemical industry in order to promote the following activities:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he production and sales of substances and mixtures of Union origin derived from sustainable carbon sources;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he use in products made available on the market of substances and mixtures of Union origin derived from sustainable carbon sources. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>In the preparation of the delegated acts, the Commission should take into account:  </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the contribution of the requirements to the Union’s objective of economic security, resilience and climate neutrality set out in Regulation (EU) 2021/1119;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the market situation at Union level, as identified through monitoring activities, including declining Union market shares and Union industry producing at below capacity</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the impact of setting such measures on the overall competitiveness and </span><span>greenhouse gas emissions of the relevant sectors, as well as on costs for downstream consumers and small and medium enterprises and public budgets.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The Commission </span><span>is empowered to </span><span>adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article </span><span>30</span><span> </span><span>in order to amend Annex II or Annex III concerning the Union origin requirements, low-carbon requirements or both set out </span><span>for products referred to therein, taking into account the following criteria:</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the market situation at Union level, as identified through monitoring activities, including declining Union market shares and Union industry producing below capacity;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>technological progress;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the contribution of the requirements to the Union’s objective of public order, economic security, resilience and climate neutrality set out in Regulation (EU) 2021/1119;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>demand for the relevant products or technologies driven by the downstream sectors’ growth;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>share of product or technology in total production value of the downstream sector; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>the impact of setting Union origin requirements, low-carbon requirements, or both on the overall competitiveness and greenhouse gas emissions of the relevant sectors</span><span>, </span><span>including</span><span> on costs for downstream consumers and small and medium enterprises and public budgets</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>The Commission </span><span>is empowered to adopt implementing acts i</span><span>n accordance with Article </span><span>31</span><span>(2)</span><span> to specify</span><span> </span><span>the method for calculating the proportion of </span><span>volume</span><span> of products and components</span><span> </span><span>originating in the Union</span><span> in accordance with </span><span>Regulation (EU) No 952/2013</span><span>, and where appropriate, </span><span>to </span><span>provide for the use of </span><span>standardised templates for certificates of compliance. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Implementing acts referred to in subparagraph 1 may also establish the methods and procedures to be applied by the relevant competent national authorities, including contracting authorities and contracting entities, to verify compliance with the requirements laid down in this Regulation and, where appropriate, to make use of digital tools for the purposes of calculation, verification and demonstration of compliance.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Normal"/>
            <p class="ChapterTitle">
               <span>CHAPTER </span><span>IV</span><span> </span><span>
                  <br/>FOREIGN INVESTMENT CONTRIBUTION</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>1</span><span>7</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Scope </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>This C</span><span>hapter shall apply to foreign direct investments</span><span> exceeding</span><span> a value of EUR 100 million in </span><span>the</span><span> emerging strategic manufacturing sectors </span><span>referred to in paragraph 2,</span><span> </span><span>where</span><span> more than 40 % of the global manufacturing capacity is held by the third country of which the foreign investor is a national or undertaking.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Such investments shall not be implemented unless explicitly approved by the Investment Authority or the European Commission, referred to in Article 19, in accordance with the provisions laid down in this Chapter.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>This chapter shall apply to foreign direct investment in manufacturing in any of the following emerging strategic sectors:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>battery technologies and its value chain for battery energy storage systems;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>pure electric vehicles, off-vehicle charging hybrid electric vehicles and fuel-cell electric vehicles, including components related to electrification</span><span> and digitalisation;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>s</span><span>olar PV technologies;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>extraction, processing and recycling of critical raw materials.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>This </span><span>C</span><span>hapter shall not apply to: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>investors and investments covered by</span><span> economic partnership and</span><span> free trade agreements in force or provisionally applied by the Union to the extent relevant commitments have been made under those agreements</span><span>,</span><span> </span><span>including investments made by the Union subsidiaries of such foreign investors;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>investments targeted at p</span><span>roviding</span><span> services</span><span>,</span><span> </span><span>including investments made by the Union subsidiaries of investors</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>portfolio investments.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>1</span><span>8</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Value added foreign direct investment criteria</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Member States shall, by [</span><span>OP</span><span> insert date: 1 month after entry into force of this Regulation], designate an </span><span>Investment Authority </span><span>which shall perform the review of foreign direct investment and </span><span>implement the provisions of this Chapter.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Member States shall provide that Investment Authority with the necessary resources, legal and administrative means for performing the tasks set out in this Regulation.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>From</span><span> [</span><span>OP</span><span> insert date: 12 month after entry into force of this Regulation], Investment Authorities shall </span><span>only </span><span>approve foreign direct investments </span><span>made directly by foreign investors </span><span>that fulfil </span><span>either four</span><span> </span><span>or more </span><span>of </span><span>the following </span><span>six </span><span>conditions</span><span>:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>f</span><span>oreign</span><span> investors </span><span>do</span><span> not acquire, hold, or exercise ownership interests representing more than 49% of the share capital, voting rights, or equivalent ownership interests in any Union target, or equivalent ownership, leasehold or other rights conferring control over a Union asset; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>f</span><span>oreign </span><span>investor</span><span> </span><span>undertakes the direct investment</span><span> through a joint venture with one or more </span><span>Union</span><span> entities, with the foreign investor </span><span>holding </span><span>no more than 49% of the</span><span> share capital, voting rights, or equivalent ownership interests or other rights conferring control </span><span>in any of the Union entities </span><span>participating in the joint venture</span><span>. Such joint ventures shall be structured to ensure effective participation of Union partners in management, technology transfer, and capacity building</span><span>;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>f</span><span>oreign investors </span><span>have</span><span> </span><span>entered into</span><span> agreements providing for the licensing of their intellectual property rights and of their know-how to the benefit of the Union Target, or the Union asset</span><span>,</span><span> to enabl</span><span>e</span><span> </span><span>it</span><span> to carry out </span><span>its</span><span> economic activities in the context of the foreign direct investment.</span><span> </span><span>All intellectual property rights or assets developed by the Union Target or the legal entity owning the Union asset prior to the foreign investment or without the collaboration of the foreign investor shall be fully and exclusively owned by the Union Target or the legal entity </span><span>of</span><span> the Union asset. All intellectual property rights or assets either developed in that context as a result of a collaboration with the foreign investor’s other business assets, or in the case of point b, developed by the joint venture, shall be owned jointly by the Foreign Investor and the Union Target, the joint venture defined in point b or the legal entity owning the Union asset</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he </span><span>f</span><span>oreign </span><span>i</span><span>nvestor annually </span><span>directs</span><span> </span><span>to research and development spending in the Union</span><span> </span><span>an amount equivalent to at least 1% of </span><span>the </span><span>gross annual revenue </span><span>of the Union target, </span><span>or the </span><span>gross annual revenue generated by the</span><span> Union asset</span><span>, as applied</span><span> </span><span>in proportion to </span><span>the foreign investor’s</span><span> share of control</span><span>;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>at least 50% of the workforce employed in the context of the foreign direct investment, at the time of its implementation and continuously throughout its operation, shall be made up of Union workers across all categories of the workforce, including operational, technical, supervisory, and managerial positions. Such employment shall be accompanied by adequate training and capacity-building measures. Where a Union target or Union asset already performing manufacturing activities before the investment is acquired, including after bankruptcy, maintaining the existing workforce or re-employment of the former workforce shall be prioritised, in accordance with national law and the application of collective agreements. In the event that the foreign investor, the Union target or the Union asset receives public funding, notwithstanding article 107 TFEU, it shall commit not to decrease the number Union workers for a period of five years on pain of recovery by the relevant national authorities, the funding awarded;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>in the context of the foreign direct investment, the foreign investor prepares and publishes on its website a strategy for enhancing Union value chains and prioritising the sourcing of inputs for the manufacturing activity from the Union and endeavours to source from the Union a minimum of 30% of inputs used for the products placed on the Union market</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>The foreign direct investment shall comply with the condition referred to in paragraph 2(e) to be approved by the Investment Authority pursuant to paragraph 2.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Investment Authorities </span><span>may</span><span> apply </span><span>some or all of </span><span>the conditions </span><span>set out</span><span> in paragraph </span><span>2</span><span> to direct investments made within the Union by a foreign investor’s subsidiary where </span><span>it is essential to achieve the objectives of this Regulation, under the following conditions</span><span>: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>preventing</span><span> the circumvention </span><span>of this Regulation by the foreign investor</span><span>;</span><span> or</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>where no alternative measures, including commitments proposed by the foreign investor or the foreign investor’s subsidiary, are reasonably available and less restrictive of direct investment within the Union in order to meet the objectives of the Regulation.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>5.</span></span><span>The Commission</span><span> shall </span><span>adopt an implementing act</span><span>, </span><span>by [OP please insert date: 6 months after entry into force of this Regulation]</span><span>)</span><span> to</span><span> </span><span>specify the detailed rules for verifying the </span><span>compliance with</span><span> the conditions </span><span>laid down in paragraph 2</span><span>.</span><span> Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in </span><span>Article </span><span>31</span><span>(3).</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>1</span><span>9</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Prior notification of planned foreign direct investments</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>A foreign investor shall notify any planned </span><span>direct</span><span> investment within the scope of Article </span><span>1</span><span>7</span><span> </span><span>to the Investment Authority of the Member State where the Union target or Union asset is located</span><span>, and</span><span> which would result in control over the Union target or Union asset as </span><span>laid down in</span><span> paragraph 3</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>The notification shall contain all necessary information to allow the Investment Authority to perform the investment review pursuant to Article 20.</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>For the purposes of determining whether the investment value</span><span> </span><span>reaches the threshold set out in Article </span><span>1</span><span>7</span><span>(1)</span><span>, </span><span>onl</span><span>y</span><span> </span><span>previous investments </span><span>of a foreign investor</span><span> made in the same Union target or Union asset by the foreign investor </span><span>from</span><span> [</span><span>OP please insert the date = the date of the entry into force of this Regulation</span><span>]</span><span> </span><span>shall be aggregated.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>Foreign investors shall be considered to have control, where the investment in question reaches </span><span>either of </span><span>the following threshold:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>3</span><span>0 percent or more share capital or voting rights in a Union target;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>3</span><span>0 percent or more of ownership of a Union asset, and leasehold or other rights conferring control over a Union asset.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Where</span><span> a foreign investor's acquisition or establishment of an investment would result in foreign investors collectively holding more than the ownership or control thresholds </span><span>laid down</span><span> </span><span>in paragraph 3, th</span><span>at acquisition or establishment</span><span> </span><span>shall</span><span> </span><span>be notified.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>5.</span></span><span>For</span><span> the purposes of calculating whether </span><span>either of </span><span>the </span><span>threshold</span><span>s</span><span> </span><span>laid down </span><span>in paragraph </span><span>3</span><span> </span><span>ha</span><span>ve</span><span> been reached</span><span>,</span><span> </span><span>aggregated </span><span>interests held directly or indirectly, including through affiliates, chains of ownership or by foreign investors acting in concert</span><span>,</span><span> shall be considered</span><span>. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>6.</span></span><span>Where the </span><span>relevant Union targets or assets are located</span><span> in more than one Member State, the foreign investor shall notify the competent Investment Authorities of all Member States </span><span>concerned</span><span> </span><span>and the Commission </span><span>on the same day with reference to the other notifications. </span><span>The</span><span> Member State</span><span>s</span><span> concerned shall coordinate the review of such notifications </span><span>and agree on the conditions imposed</span><span> with the other Member States concerned</span><span>, as well as with the Commission</span><span>. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>The Commission shall decide which conditions shall be applied to the foreign direct investment in case there is no agreement between the Member States concerned.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Foreign direct investment notified pursuant to the first subparagraph shall fulfil the conditions laid down in Article 18 in all Member States concerned. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>20</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Review and approval</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The Investment Authority shall decide on the admissibility of the notification </span><span>pursuant to </span><span>Article</span><span>s </span><span>1</span><span>7</span><span> and</span><span> </span><span>1</span><span>9</span><span> within 30 days of receiving the notification. Th</span><span>at</span><span> deadline may be extended by a further 15 days where </span><span>the Investment Authority demonstrates satisfactorily that an extension is</span><span> justified by the circumstances.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Where the Investment Authority decides a notification is admissible, it shall immediately transmit the full notification to the Commission including all documents received.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>Within 30 days after receiving the notification, the Commission may issue a written opinion on whether the foreign direct investment falls within the scope of Articles 1</span><span>7</span><span> and 1</span><span>9</span><span>, whether it fulfils the conditions laid out in Article 1</span><span>8</span><span>(2), and whether the Investment Authority is to approve the investment or not. </span>
