            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Where the Commission issues a written opinion, it shall transmit it to the Investment Authority without delay. The Commission may share the written opinion with the Investment Authorities of other Member States or publish the written opinion on its official website, with due regard to confidentiality. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>No sooner than</span><span> receiving the opinion of the Commission or the lapse of the deadline</span><span> </span><span>referred to in paragraph 2</span><span> and no later than 60 days</span><span>, or 75 days if the deadline was extended in accordance with paragraph 1,</span><span> after receipt of the notification, the Investment Authority shall issue a reasoned decision approving or declining the foreign direct investment. </span><span>The Investment Authority shall approve the foreign direct investment if it fulfils </span><span>4</span><span> out of 6 conditions set out in Article </span><span>1</span><span>8</span><span>. The deadline for issuing the reasoned decision may be extended by a further 30 days where the Investment Authority demonstrates satisfactorily that an extension is justified by the circumstances.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>The Investment Authority shall communicate such reasoned decisions to the Commission within three days of adoption.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Where the Investment Authority gives a decision which diverts from the Commission opinion as regards compliance of the foreign direct investment with the conditions laid down in Article 1</span><span>8</span><span>, the Investment Authority shall assess the notification in greater detail within</span><span> </span><span>an additional period of two months</span><span> and the decision shall only enter into force after the lapse of this deadline</span><span>. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Investment Authorities shall, in their reasoned decision issued pursuant to paragraph 3, justify how the opinion of the Commission was taken into account.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>5.</span></span><span>The Investment Authority shall, in its approval decision, set out reporting obligations on the investor concerned, with a view to assessing the </span><span>continuous</span><span> fulfilment of the conditions laid down in </span><span>Article 1</span><span>8</span><span>. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>6.</span></span><span>Any party subject to a decision issued pursuant to paragraphs 1 or 3 shall have the right to seek judicial recourse against such decision.</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>21</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Review of foreign direct </span><span>investment</span><span> by the Commission</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Following the notification referred to in Article </span><span>19</span><span>(1), the Commission may decide</span><span> to undertake the assessment of the foreign direct investment in the following circumstances:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>on </span><span>its own initiative, where</span><span> the foreign direct investment has the potential to significantly </span><span>impact</span><span> </span><span>added value creation in the Union market</span><span>;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>on </span><span>the request of an Investment Authority handling </span><span>a</span><span> notification, or an Investment Authority of another Member State</span><span>,</span><span> </span><span>in which</span><span> the foreign direct investment </span><span>in question </span><span>would have </span><span>a </span><span>significant impact on </span><span>its</span><span> territory</span><span>; or</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>on its own initiative, where the</span><span> foreign direct investment </span><span>has value</span><span> exceeding EUR</span><span> 1 b</span><span>illion</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>For the purposes of paragraph 1, the foreign direct investment shall be deemed to have the potential to significantly impact the added value creation in the internal market, in any of the following cases:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>it is </span><span>of particular strategic importance for the </span><span>internal </span><span>market;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>it has considerable economic impact</span><span> </span><span>on</span><span> the territory of more than one Member State;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>it has high potential of disrupting the security of supply of that emerging strategic sector or related value chains in the Union, or security in more than one Member State; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>it has high potential of having detrimental environmental effect in more than one Member State; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>it is </span><span>of a </span><span>particularly</span><span> high value </span><span>compared to</span><span> </span><span>other </span><span>investments in that emerging strategic sector.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>Following the </span><span>notification </span><span>referred </span><span>to </span><span>in </span><span>Article </span><span>19</span><span>(1), </span><span>the Commission may decide to undertake the assessment of an investment referred to in Article 1</span><span>8</span><span>(</span><span>4). The Commission may carry out its assessment on its own initiative, or at the request of </span><span>an Investment Authority handling </span><span>a</span><span> notification, or an Investment Authority of another Member State </span><span>on which</span><span> the foreign direct investment </span><span>in question </span><span>would have </span><span>a </span><span>significant impact</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Based on its assessment, the Commission may require the Investment Authority to apply in a proportionate manner, or not to apply, some or all the conditions set out in Article18(2). </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Where</span><span> the Commission decides to </span><span>assess</span><span> the foreign direct investment pursuant to </span><span>this</span><span> Article</span><span>, </span><span>the </span><span>provisions </span><span>set out in </span><span>Article </span><span>18</span><span> </span><span>shall</span><span> apply, mutatis mutandis, starting from its decision to undertake the assessment</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>22</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Monitoring and enforcement</span><span> by the Investment Authority</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The Investment Authority shall regularly monitor the foreign direct investment </span><span>to ensure that it </span><span>continues to fulfil the conditions laid down in </span><span>Article </span><span>1</span><span>8</span><span>.</span><span> For th</span><span>at</span><span> purpose, the foreign investor shall regularly report to the Investment Authority on compliance with the conditions. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>Upon request by the Commission, the Investment Authority shall transmit the investor’s reports </span><span>submitted pursuant to paragraph 1</span><span> to the Commission together with its own assessment on each report.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>The Investment Authority shall establish penalties in case of non-compliance with the provisions of this Chapter, in particular </span><span>where foreign investors or investments fail to comply with the following </span><span>requirements</span><span>: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the notification requirements</span><span> in accordance with Article </span><span>1</span><span>9</span><span>; </span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the conditions laid down in Article </span><span>1</span><span>8</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the monitoring obligations established by this Article.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Penalty payments established by the Investment Authority shall </span><span>not amount to less than</span><span> 5</span><span> </span><span>% of the average daily aggregate turnover of the foreign investor undertaking</span><span> in case of a violation pursuant to paragraph 3, point (a)</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Where the foreign investor is a private person, the Investment Authority shall establish a penalty payment of at least 5 % of the investment value in case a violation pursuant to paragraph 3, point (a).</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>The penalty payments established by the Investment Authority shall be effective and proportionate to the violations laid down in paragraph 3.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>The Investment Authority shall inform the Commission without undue delay of any non-compliance referred to in paragraph 3 and of the consequential penalties imposed.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>3</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Monitoring </span><span>by the Commission</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>For the purposes of </span><span>Article </span><span>1</span><span>7</span><span>,</span><span> the Commission shall monitor the global manufacturing capacity for each of the emerging strategic sectors, building on existing monitoring activities performed, in particular pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2024/1735.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The Commission shall provide and publish updated information on the most recent year for which data is available for each of the emerging strategic sectors referred to in Article</span><span> </span><span>1</span><span>7</span><span>(2</span><span>)</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>Where the Commission decides to assess the foreign direct investment pursuant to Article 21, it may by decision impose penalties if the foreign investor provides false or misleading information in their notification, or if it does not supply the information required for the Commission to perform its review obligation.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>The penalties imposed by the Commission shall not exceed the 5% average daily turnover of the foreign investor, or in case of a private person foreign investor, 5% of the investment value. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>4</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Delegat</span><span>ion of powers</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The Commission is empowered to adopt </span><span>delegated acts</span><span> in accordance with Article </span><span>30</span><span> of this Regulation </span><span>to </span><span>supplement</span><span> the list of emerging strategic sectors to be covered by this </span><span>C</span><span>hapter to sectors critical to the Union’s economic security</span><span> </span><span>including</span><span> </span><span>net-zero</span><span> technologies listed in Article 4(1), points (b), (d), (e), (g), (h), (j), (k), (n), (p), and (s), </span><span>of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735</span><span>, </span><span>nuclear fuel cycle technologies referred to in Article 4(1), point (i), </span><span>of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735</span><span>, </span><span>electric propulsion technologies for transport referred to in Article 4(1), point (r</span><span>), of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735</span><span>, and excluding digital technologies, artificial intelligence</span><span>, quantum technologies</span><span> and semiconductors.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text1">
               <span>These delegated acts shall be without prejudice to other Union acts establishing investment criteria for these sectors.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The</span><span> </span><span>delegated </span><span>acts referred to</span><span> in paragraph </span><span>1</span><span> </span><span>shall be based </span><span>on the following</span><span> factors</span><span>: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>an assessment </span><span>of</span><span> </span><span>whether </span><span>modifying the list of emerging strategic sectors would</span><span> unduly deter or discourag</span><span>e</span><span> foreign direct investment in the Union;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>number</span><span> </span><span>of foreign direct investments in that sector</span><span>, </span><span>taking into account </span><span>their contribution to the Union’s security of supply</span><span> and their added value to the Union’s economy;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>market situation and conditions</span><span>, including supply chain disturbances,</span><span> on Union level</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>technological developments and the Union’s competitiveness in that sector</span><span> in comparison </span><span>to </span><span>third countries</span><span>; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>supply chain dependence </span><span>i</span><span>n the relevant sector </span><span>on one </span><span>or more</span><span> countr</span><span>ies</span><span>.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>The </span><span>delegated </span><span>acts</span><span> adopted pursuant to paragraph </span><span>1</span><span> shall contain</span><span>:</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he threshold value referred to in </span><span>Article </span><span>1</span><span>7</span><span>(1)</span><span> for each of </span><span>those</span><span> additional sectors;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>whether the investment </span><span>c</span><span>onditions</span><span> referred to in Article </span><span>1</span><span>8</span><span> are appropriate and necessary to meet the objectives </span><span>of this </span><span>Regulation </span><span>with</span><span> respect to the sector concerned</span><span>, and if not, which of </span><span>those</span><span> criteria </span><span>is to </span><span>be applied.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="ChapterTitle">
               <span>CHAPTER V</span><span>
                  <br/>INDUSTRIAL </span><span>MANUFACTURING </span><span>ACCELERATION AREA</span><span>S</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 2</span><span>5</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Designating national </span><span>industrial manufacturing acceleration areas</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Member States shall designate at least one</span><span> </span><span>industrial </span><span>manufacturing </span><span>acceleration area on their territory by [OP please insert date: 12 months following the entry into force of this Regulation] </span><span>to cluster </span><span>industrial manufacturing project</span><span>s </span><span>in </span><span>one or several of the s</span><span>trategic sectors listed in Annex I</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>Member States shall designate </span><span>industrial manufacturing acceleration areas</span><span> </span><span>by decision, </span><span>on the basis of the following elements:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the impact of the </span><span>i</span><span>ndustrial manufacturing</span><span> </span><span>acceleration area's production on the security of the Union's supply for </span><span>the </span><span>strategic sectors</span><span> listed in Annex I</span><span>; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the potential of the </span><span>industrial manufacturing </span><span>acceleration area to support the deployment of product</span><span>ion capacity</span><span> in </span><span>the </span><span>strategic sectors</span><span> listed in Annex I</span><span>, </span><span>to </span><span>strengthen Union value chains</span><span> and</span><span> the </span><span>Union</span><span>’s innovation potential </span><span>to accelerate </span><span>sustainable manufacturing </span><span>industrial </span><span>activities</span><span>,</span><span> including </span><span>decarbonisation</span><span> </span><span>and circular business practices,</span><span> </span><span>and </span><span>to</span><span> foster </span><span>the functioning of</span><span> the internal market, in alignment with strategic projects </span><span>and other initiatives</span><span>, including</span><span> as Net Zero </span><span>Acceleration </span><span>Valleys</span><span>,</span><span> </span><span>carried out pursuant to other Union legislation; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the </span><span>number of SMEs and SMCs that would</span><span> benefit from the provisions of this Chapter within the </span><span>industrial</span><span> acceleration area</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>the Member </span><span>State’s regions’</span><span> level of development</span><span>, </span><span>including </span><span>least developed areas, regions in transition, and those undergoing industrial transformation</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>When designating industrial manufacturing acceleration areas, Member States shall: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>define</span><span> a clear geographic scope for the acceleration area; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>prioritise </span><span>locations </span><span>where the deployment of a specific sector or sectors of industrial manufacturing </span><span>project</span><span>s</span><span> </span><span>is not expected to have a significant environmental impact;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>prioritise </span><span>locations outside </span><span>Natura 2000 sites and </span><span>outside </span><span>areas designated under national protection schemes for nature and biodiversity conservation, as well as other areas identified on the basis of sensitivity maps</span><span> and outside protected areas as referred to in Article 6 of Directive 2000/60/EC;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>take into account climate risks in the areas designated;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>prioritis</span><span>e</span><span> artificial and built surfaces, industrial sites, and brownfield sites</span><span>, as well as </span><span>already identifie</span><span>d</span><span> strategic projects pursuant to other Union legislation</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>When designating </span><span>industrial manufacturing acceleration areas</span><span>, Member States shall</span><span> </span><span>take into account</span><span>, as relevant, the following considerations</span><span>:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the infrastructural needs of the acceleration area;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the financing needs of manufacturing industry located in the acceleration area </span><span>and the possibility to support that industry, where applicable</span><span>,</span><span> in </span><span>accordance with</span><span> </span><span>applicable State aid rules;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the supply chain needs within the acceleration area and the essential materials</span><span>, particularly secondary materials,</span><span> necessary for manufacturing activities;</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>the feasibility of connecting the acceleration area with sufficient </span><span>low-carbon </span><span>energy supply for the acceleration of industrial </span><span>manufacturing </span><span>activity; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>skill needs, the shortages and employment trends and support measures to achieve the adequate reskilling and upskilling of the local workforce;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>the need, as relevant, for depollution of the acceleration area to facilitate the commencement of new industrial activities;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(g)</span></span><span>research and innovation needs for accelerating the manufacturing industrial activity in the area</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(h)</span></span><span>relevant location-specific information made publicly available by industry, including corporate climate transition plans, related targets and actions, investment needs, and required enabling policy frameworks</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>5.</span></span><span>Before their adoption, the </span><span>plans or programmes on</span><span> the designat</span><span>ion of the industrial manufacturing acceleration areas</span><span> shall be subject to an environmental assessment pursuant to Directive 2001/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref63" href="#footnote63">63</a>
               </span><span>, and, if they are likely to have a significant impact on Natura 2000 sites, to the appropriate assessment pursuant to Article 6(3) of </span><span>Council </span><span>Directive 92/43/EEC</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref64" href="#footnote64">64</a>
               </span><span> </span><span>and, where applicable, to the relevant assessment to comply with Article 4(7) of </span><span>Directive 2000</span><span>/60/EC</span><span> </span><span>of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref65" href="#footnote65">65</a>
               </span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>6.</span></span><span>Member States shall</span><span> inform the Commission of the designation of an industrial manufacturing acceleration area</span><span>, within 30 days from the </span><span>adoption of the relevant </span><span>decision.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>6</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Enabling conditions</span>
            </p>
            <p class="NumPar11">
               <span>Member States shall take the following measures, where appropriate, to facilitate the development of industrial manufacturing acceleration areas:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>facilitate financing of projects in the acceleration areas </span><span>by ensuring coordination between authorities and streamlining </span><span>internal procedures, </span><span>in synergy with Union programmes</span><span> and in </span><span>accordance </span><span>with existing State aid rules where applicable</span><span>, taking into account the participation of SMEs and SMCs;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>p</span><span>romote</span><span> </span><span>research and innovation</span><span> investments to accelerate the innovative potential and </span><span>Union</span><span>’s competitiveness and technology leadership in the acceleration areas;</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>conduct, and</span><span> </span><span>review at least ever</span><span>y</span><span> three years, a comprehensive analysis of the </span><span>energy </span><span>needs of </span><span>each accel</span><span>eration area</span><span> and </span><span>identifying </span><span>the required </span><span>energy infrastructure capacity</span><span> for </span><span>the proper functioning and development of </span><span>industrial manufacturing projects</span><span> located in the acceleration area. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text2">
               <span>Such analysis shall be conducted, at least, when designating the industrial acceleration area and for the milestones of years 2030, 2040 and 2050, ensuring alignment with the Union’s decarbonisation pathway;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>ensure that the network development plans prepared by transmission system operators pursuant to Article 51 of Directive (EU) 2019/944 </span><span>of the European Parliament and of the Council</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref66" href="#footnote66">66</a>
               </span><span> </span><span>and distribution system operators pursuant to Article 32 of Directive (EU) 2019/944 take due account of the analysis prepared pursuant to </span><span>point (</span><span>c</span><span>) of this paragraph</span><span>, considering the potential of anticipatory investments to accommodate future system needs;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>exchange information on relevant supply chains, identify potential bottlenecks, and strengthen coordination between acceleration areas on critical raw materials issues within the framework of the European Critical Raw Materials Board established by Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1252;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>promote entities in the acceleration areas and facilitate their participation, where relevant, in the joint purchasing mechanism established by Article 25 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1252, including by providing guidance, support, and information to ensure effective engagement;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(g)</span></span><span>support the development and availability of a highly skilled workforce and provide appropriate training and apprenticeship opportunities, thereby contributing to high-quality employment within those acceleration areas; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(h)</span></span><span>exchange information on the </span><span>necessary </span><span>skills, potential shortages </span><span>of those skills </span><span>and best practices applied in the acceleration areas within the framework of the Industrial Forum expert group established by COM/2020/102</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref67" href="#footnote67">67</a>
               </span><span>; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(i)</span></span><span>ensure synergies and promote the benefits provided under the Pact for Skills</span><span class="FootnoteReference">
                  <a class="footnoteRef" id="footnoteref68" href="#footnote68">68</a>
               </span><span> or entities established in the acceleration areas, with particular attention to Large-Scale Skill Partnerships and Regional Skills Partnerships included therein.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>7</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Permit-granting procedure</span><span>s</span><span> in acceleration areas</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>For each designated </span><span>industrial manufacturing </span><span>acceleration area, Member States shall prepare and issue an aggregated baseline permit authorising industrial </span><span>activities</span><span> located within that area</span><span>. </span><span>This aggregated baseline permit shall cover the permits and</span><span> </span><span>administrative authorisations required for </span><span>the industrial manufacturing projects located within the acceleration area, </span><span>excluding those permits that are installation specific</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>Before </span><span>issuing</span><span> the aggregated baseline permit referred to in paragraph 1, </span><span>Member</span><span> States shall carry out all necessary assessments, including relevant environmental assessments, planning procedures and evaluations applicable at the level of the acceleration area.</span><span> </span><span>Member States shall take into account </span><span>the assessment carried out pursuant to </span><span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>5</span><span>(5).</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>Industrial </span><span>manufacturing</span><span> projects located within an </span><span>industrial manufacturing </span><span>acceleration</span><span> area shall be required to obtain only those additional permits or authorisations that fall outside the scope of the aggregated baseline permit referred to in paragraph 1.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>All </span><span>industrial manufacturing projects located within an acceleration area shall be considered strategic projects </span><span>contributing to resilience and </span><span>de</span><span>carbonisation or resource efficiency</span><span> </span><span>for the purposes</span><span> of </span><span>[</span><span>Article 14 of</span><span> </span><span>Proposal for a Regulation on speeding-up environmental assessment</span><span>]</span><span>.</span><span> </span><span>Points 1, 2 and 3 of the Annex </span><span>to</span><span> that Regulation shall apply.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="ChapterTitle">
               <span>CHAPTER VI</span><span>
                  <br/>FINAL PROVISIONS</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>8</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Evaluation</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>By [OP: Please insert the date = two years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation], and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Regulation and of its contribution to the functioning of the internal market. The evaluation shall consider: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>progress made in achieving </span><span>the objectives specified in Article 1, particularly on resilience, economic security and decarbonisation of industrial production; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>progress made in achieving </span><span>the industrialisation objective </span><span>pursuant to</span><span> </span><span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>, taking into account the challenges and opportunities in the internal market</span><span> </span><span>and global markets</span><span>;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the related administrative costs, economic impacts on downstream sectors, small and medium enterprises and impacts on public budgets</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>2</span><span>9</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Review</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>By [OP: Please insert the date three years after the date of entry into force this Regulation], the Commission shall assess the necessity of amending Chapters III and IV. The Commission may submit a legislative proposal in order to repeal or amend this Regulation. That review shall be carried out periodically every three years after the first review. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>When carrying out its review, the Commission shall pay particular attention to the effectiveness of this Regulation and the persistence of the circumstances that have justified the adoption of this Regulation and to the necessity to introduce Union origin requirements for products from certain sectors critical to the Union’s economic security, notably the building of ships and of rail rolling stock.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>30</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Exercise of the delegation</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The power to adopt delegated acts referred to </span><span>in Articles </span><span>8, 9, 10, 16 and 24</span><span>shall be conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period of time from [OP please insert the date = the date of the entry into force of this Regulation].</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>The delegation of power referred to in Articles </span><span>8, 9, 10, 16 and 24 </span><span>may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council. A decision to revoke shall put an end to the delegation of the power specified in that decision. It shall take effect on the day following the publication of the decision in the Official Journal of the European Union or at a later date specified therein. It shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State in accordance with the principles laid down in the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016 on Better Law-Making.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>5.</span></span><span>As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission shall notify it simultaneously to the European Parliament and to the Council.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>6.</span></span><span>A delegated act adopted pursuant to Articles </span><span>8, 9, 10, 16 and 24</span><span>shall enter into force only if no objection has been expressed either by the European Parliament</span><span> or by the Council within a period of two months of notification of that act to the European Parliament and the Council or if, before the expiry of that period, the European Parliament and the Council have both informed the Commission that they will not object. That period shall be extended by two months at the initiative of the European Parliament or of the Council.</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>31</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Committee procedure</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The Commission shall be assisted by a Committee. That Committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>Where reference is made to this paragraph, Article 4 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 shall apply.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>Where reference is made to this paragraph, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 shall apply.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>32</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Penalties</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>Member States shall lay down rules on penalties applicable to infringements of the provisions of this Regulation and shall take all necessary measures to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive. Member States shall, without delay, notify the Commission of those rules and measures and shall notify it, without delay, of any subsequent amendment affecting them.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>3</span><span>3</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>Annexes I and II to Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 are amended in accordance with Annex V to this Regulation. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article </span><span>3</span><span>4</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 is amended as follows:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(1)</span></span><span>in </span><span>Article 3</span><span> the following points (34), (35) and (36) are added:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span> </span><span>‘(</span><span>34) </span><span>‘industrial battery’ means </span><span>an industrial battery as defined in Article 3(1), point (13), of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542</span><span> of the European Parliament and the </span><span>C</span><span>ouncil</span><span>*</span><span>;’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span> ‘</span><span>(35) </span><span>‘stationary battery energy storage system’ </span><span>means </span><span>a</span><span> </span><span>stationary battery energy storage system</span><span> </span><span>as defined in Article 3(1), point (15), of Regulation (EU) 2023/</span><span>1542</span><span>;’</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span> ‘</span><span>(36) </span><span>‘hydronic heat pump’ means a space heater using ambient heat from an air source, water source or ground source, and/or waste heat for heat generation and heating space through a water circuit</span><span>.</span><span>’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span>___</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span>* Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 July 2023 concerning batteries and waste batteries, amending Directive 2008/98/EC and Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and repealing Directive 2006/66/EC (OJ L 191, 28.7.2023, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1542/oj).;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(2)</span></span><span>i</span><span>n Article 9, </span><span>the following</span><span> </span><span>paragraph </span><span>(</span><span>14</span><span>)</span><span> is </span><span>added</span><span>: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span>14. All net-zero technology manufacturing projects shall be considered strategic projects contributing to resilience and decarbonisation or resource efficiency for the purpose of Article 14(1) of [Proposal for a Regulation on speeding-up environmental assessment].’;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(3)</span></span><span>Article 25 is amended as follows: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>paragraph 1 is replaced by </span><span>the following: </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span>‘1. For public procurement procedures falling within the scope of Directive 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU or 2014/25/EU, where contracts have net-zero technologies listed in Article 4(1), points (a) to (d), (h) and (i), of this Regulation as part of their subject matter, or in the case of works contracts and works concessions including said technology, contracting authorities and contracting entities shall apply minimum mandatory requirements regarding environmental sustainability established in the implementing act referred to in paragraph 5 of this Article.’;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>i</span><span>n paragraph 7</span><span>, the </span><span>first subparagraph</span><span> is replaced by</span><span> the following:</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span>‘The tender’s resilience contribution shall be taken into account in the case of public procurement procedures, work contracts and works concessions referred to in paragraph 1, in accordance with this paragraph.’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>in paragraph 7, </span><span>point (a) is replaced by the following: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span>‘(a) an obligation for the duration of the contract not to supply more than 50 % of the value of the specific net-zero technology final product referred to in this paragraph from each individual third country as determined by the Commission;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>in paragraph 7, point (b) is replaced by the following: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span>‘(b) an obligation for the duration of the contract that no more than 50 % of the value of all the main specific components of the specific net-zero technology referred to in this paragraph taken together is supplied or provided directly by the successful tenderer or by a subcontractor from each individual third country as determined by the Commission;’;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(4)</span></span><span>The following Article </span><span>25a </span><span>is</span><span> </span><span>inserted: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>‘Article </span><span>25</span><span>a</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Origin requirements for public procurement </span><span>procedures</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>For</span><span> public procurement procedures referred to in Annex II, contracting authorities and contracting entities shall exclude from access to such procurement procedures tenders </span><span>submitted by</span><span> </span><span>economic operators </span><span>owned or controlled by an entity established in </span><span>third countries</span><span> which have not concluded an international agreement with the Union guaranteeing such access.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>For p</span><span>ublic procurement procedures referred to in Annex II</span><span>, contracting authorities and contracting entities</span><span> shall </span><span>apply</span><span> the</span><span> Union origin requirements laid down therein.</span><span> </span><span>Requirements relating to specific main specific components shall only apply to the </span><span>extent that those components are included in the final product.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>Contracting authorities and contracting entities may decide not to apply </span><span>one or several </span><span>requirements set out in </span><span>Annex II</span><span> </span><span>where any of the following conditions are fulfilled: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the required products can only be supplied by one specific economic operator, and no reasonable alternative or substitute exists, and the absence of competition is not the result of an artificial narrowing down of the parameters of the public procurement procedure;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>no suitable tenders or no suitable requests to participate have been submitted, including in response to a similar former public procurement procedure launched by the same contracting authority or contracting entity in the two years preceding the start of the planned new procurement procedure;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>their application would require a contracting authority or contracting entity to acquire goods, services or works having disproportionate costs or would result in technical incompatibility in operation and maintenance. Estimated cost differences </span><span>in excess of</span><span> </span><span>25</span><span>%, based on objective and transparent data, may be presumed by contracting authorities and contracting entities to be disproportionate.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>their</span><span> application would lead to significant delays </span><span>to the delivery of the project</span><span> </span><span>due to the unavailability of the required components</span><span> or final products</span><span>.</span><span> </span><span>Estimated d</span><span>elays in excess of </span><span>seven </span><span>months</span><span>, based on objective</span><span>, transparent</span><span> and verif</span><span>iable data,</span><span> may be presumed to be significant.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>Contracting authorities shall require economic operators supplying products falling within the scope of this </span><span>Article</span><span> </span><span>to submit a self-declaration, or an equivalent document, demonstrating compliance with the requirements set out in this </span><span>Article</span><span>.</span><span>’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(5)</span></span><span>Article 26 is amended as follows: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he </span><span>heading</span><span> </span><span>is replaced by </span><span>the following: </span><span>‘Auctions for net-zero technologies’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>paragraph 1 is </span><span>amended as follows: </span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point2">
               <span>the introductory wording is replaced by the following: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point2">
               <span>‘When designing auctions for net-zero technologies listed in Article 4(1), points (a) to (g), (i) and (j), Member states shall include:’ </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point2">
               <span>in point (a), the following point (iv) is added: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point2">
               <span>‘ (iv) high-risk suppliers as defined in Article 2 point (39) of Regulation xxxx/xxxx [CSA2]: For auctions that include control systems, management control systems, supervisory control and data acquisition systems, remote access systems or firewalls, suppliers identified as high-risk suppliers in accordance with Regulation xxxx/xxxx [CSA2]shall not be involved in the following processes:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point3">
               <span class="num"><span>(1)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he supply of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point3">
               <span class="num"><span>(2)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he design, development or production of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point3">
               <span class="num"><span>(3)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he management, control or operation of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point3">
               <span class="num"><span>(4)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he development, maintenance, operation, or updating of their software</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point2">
               <span>point (b), is replaced by the following: ‘pre-qualification criteria or award criteria as referred to in paragraphs 2 and 2a’.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>The following paragraph 2a is inserted: ‘2a. Where the auctions have net-zero technologies listed in Annex II as part of their subject-matter, Member States shall include the pre-qualification or award criteria laid down in Annex II</span><span>.</span><span>’</span><span> </span><span>Criteria relating to specific main specific components shall only apply to the extent that those components are included in the final product.’; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>i</span><span>n paragraph 3, </span><span>the first </span><span>sub</span><span>paragraph is replaced by </span><span>the following: ‘</span><span>The Commission is empowered to adopt</span><span> </span><span>an implementing act further specifying </span><span>the pre-qualification and award</span><span> </span><span>criteria referred to in</span><span> paragraph 1</span><span>points </span><span>(a), (i)</span><span>, (ii)</span><span> and</span><span> </span><span>(iii)</span><span>,</span><span> and paragraph 2</span><span>.</span><span>’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>paragraph 4</span><span> </span><span>is replaced by </span><span>the following:</span><span> ‘</span><span>4. </span><span>Member States shall give to each of the</span><span> </span><span>criteria referred to in paragraphs 2 and 2</span><span>a</span><span>, when applied as award criteria, a minimum weight of 5 % and a combined weight of between 15 % and 30 % of the award criteria. </span><span>That</span><span> is without prejudice to the possibility to give a higher weighting to the criteria referred to in the fourth subparagraph of paragraph 2, in accordance with any limit for non-price criteria set </span><span>out in</span><span> State aid rules.</span><span>’.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>p</span><span>aragraph 5 is replaced by </span><span>the following:</span><span> ‘</span><span>5. </span><span>Member States shall not be </span><span>required</span><span> </span><span>to apply </span><span>one or several of</span><span> the pre-qualification and award criteria laid down in paragraph 1</span><span>, points </span><span>(a), (i)</span><span>, (ii) and</span><span> </span><span>(iii), and paragraph 1</span><span>, point </span><span>(b)</span><span>,</span><span> where</span><span> the application of </span><span>those criteria</span><span> </span><span>would </span><span>result in</span><span> </span><span>disproportionate costs</span><span> or </span><span>in </span><span>significant delays</span><span> </span><span>to the delivery of the project</span><span> due to the unavailability of </span><span>the required </span><span>components</span><span> or final products</span><span>. Estimated cost differences </span><span>in excess of</span><span> </span><span>2</span><span>0</span><span>% per auction, based on objective and verifiable data, may be presumed by Member States to be disproportionate.</span><span> </span><span>Delays </span><span>in excess of</span><span> </span><span>seven</span><span> month</span><span>s</span><span>, based on</span><span> objective, transparent and verifiable data,</span><span> may be presumed to be </span><span>significant.</span><span>’ </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(g)</span></span><span>paragraph 7 is replaced by </span><span>the following: </span><span>‘</span><span>7. Paragr</span><span>aphs 1 to 5</span><span> </span><span>shall apply to at least </span><span>4</span><span>0% of the volume auctioned per year per Member State</span><span> or alternatively to at least </span><span>8</span><span> </span><span>Gigawatt per year per Member State</span><span>.</span><span> </span><span>Paragraph 1</span><span>, points </span><span>(a)(ii) and (iv)</span><span>,</span><span> shall apply to 100% of the volume auctioned per Member State</span><span>.</span><span>’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(h)</span></span><span>in</span><span> paragraph 8</span><span>, the introductory wording</span><span> is replaced by</span><span> the following</span><span>: ‘By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall carry out a comprehensive assessment of the application of the criteria referred to in paragraph 2 and their effect on the accelerated deployment of renewable energy technologies. By 31 December 2029 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out a comprehensive assessment of the application of the criteria referred to in paragraphs 2 and 2</span><span>a</span><span> and their effect on the accelerated deployment of renewable energy technologies. In particular, the Commission shall assess the impact of the criteria on:’</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
               <span class="num"><span>(6)</span></span><span>The following </span><span>A</span><span>rticles </span><span>28a to 28</span><span>e</span><span> are inserted:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28</span><span>a</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Origin requirements for </span><span>other forms of public intervention</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Without prejudice to Articles 107 and 108 TFEU, support schemes referred to in Annex II shall include the requirements laid down therein.</span><span> Requirements relating to specific main specific components shall only apply to the extent that those components are included in the final product.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>When designing and implementing a scheme pursuant to paragraph 1, the authority shall assess the </span><span>fulfilment of the </span><span>requirements on the basis of an open, non-discriminatory and transparent process.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>When additional financial compensation is granted, it shall </span><span>not exceed </span><span>15% of the cost of the final product for the consumer, including transport and installation costs where relevant</span><span>, with the e</span><span>xception of schemes targeting citizens living in energy poverty, as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Regulation (EU) 2023/955 of the European Parliament and of the Council </span>
               <a class="externalRef"
                  href="https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1735/oj/eng">
                  <span class="Hyperlink">(</span><span class="Hyperlink">57</span><span class="Hyperlink">)</span>
               </a>
               <span>, for which the limit shall be </span><span>2</span><span>0</span><span> %.</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28</span><span>b</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Limitations to high-risk suppliers for other forms of public intervention</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Text0">
               <span>For support schemes within the scope of Articles 28 and 28a that include control systems, management control systems, supervisory control and data acquisition systems, remote access systems or firewalls, Member States shall design those schemes in such a way as to ensure that beneficiaries shall be eligible to the scheme only where suppliers identified as high-risk suppliers in accordance with Regulation xxxx/xxxx [CSA2] are not be involved in the following processes: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he supply of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he design, development or production of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he management, control or operation of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he development, maintenance, operation, or updating of their software. </span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28</span><span>c</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Union origin requirements for Member State support to </span><span>construction and </span><span>manufacturing</span><span> of net-zero technologies</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>Without prejudice to Articles 107 and 108 TFEU and in </span><span>accordance</span><span> </span><span>with the Union’s international commitments, when supporting the </span><span>construction</span><span> </span><span>or </span><span>manufacturing of net-zero technology final products referred to in Annex II</span><span> of this Regulation</span><span>, Member States shall ensure that the Union origin requirements laid down in </span><span>that A</span><span>nnex are met.</span><span> Requirements relating to specific main specific components shall only apply to the extent that those components are included in the final product.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>Member States may decide not to apply </span><span>one or several requirements referred to in </span><span>paragraph 1 </span><span>where</span><span> any of the following </span><span>conditions are fulfilled</span><span>: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the required components can only be supplied by one specific economic operator, and no reasonable alternative or substitute exists, and the absence of competition is not the result of an artificial narrowing down of the parameters of the public procurement procedure;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>their</span><span> application would result in </span><span>disproportionate costs or </span><span>technical incompatibility in operation or maintenance</span><span>. Estimated cost differences </span><span>in excess of</span><span> </span><span>25</span><span>%, based on objective and transparent data, may be presumed to be disproportionate</span><span>; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>their</span><span> application would jeopardise the project or lead to significant delays </span><span>to the delivery of the project </span><span>due to the unavailability of the required components</span><span> or final products</span><span>. </span><span>Delays in excess of </span><span>seven </span><span>months</span><span>, based on objective, transparent and verifiable data,</span><span> may be presumed to be significant.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>Without prejudice to Articles 107 and 108 TFEU</span><span> and in </span><span>accordance</span><span> </span><span>with the Union’s international commitments</span><span>, when supporting the manufacturing of net-zero technology final products referred to in Annex II </span><span>of this Regulation </span><span>and that include control systems, management control systems, supervisory control and data acquisition systems, remote access systems or firewalls, Member States shall ensure that suppliers identified as high-risk </span><span>suppliers </span><span>in accordance with </span><span>Regulation xxxx/xxxx [CSA2]</span><span> </span><span>are not involved in</span><span> the following processes</span><span>:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he supply of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he design, development or production of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he management, control or operation of those products or systems; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>t</span><span>he development, maintenance, operation, or updating of their software.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28</span><span>d</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Union origin</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>For the purposes of Articles 25</span><span>a</span><span>, 26 and 28</span><span>a</span><span> </span><span>and</span><span> </span><span>28</span><span>c</span><span>, </span><span>content of Union origin refers to content originating in the Union.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The</span><span> </span><span>origin of products </span><span>and components </span><span>shall be determined in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 of the European Parliament.</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28e</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Content equivalent to Union origin in public procurement</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>With respect to the Union origin requirements referred to in Article </span><span>25a</span><span>, content originating in third countries with which the Union has concluded an agreement establishing a free trade area or a customs union, or that are parties to the Agreement on Government Procurement</span><span>, where relevant obligations of the Union exist under that agreement, </span><span> shall be deemed to be of Union origin </span><span>.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The Commission </span><span>shall </span><span>adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article </span><span>44</span><span> to exclude, in whole or in part, a third country from the scope of paragraph 1 based on any of the following criteria: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>that third country has failed to provide national treatment related to Union products or entities under the agreements referred to in paragraph 1 in relation to any of the net-zero technologies listed in Article 4, point (1);</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(f)</span></span><span>such exclusion is justified to avoid dependencies or any other developments that may threaten the security of supply in the Union of the products in question;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(g)</span></span><span>such exclusion</span><span> is justified under any other exception under the applicable agreement</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28f</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Content equivalent to Union origin in auctions</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>3.</span></span><span>With respect to the Union origin requirements referred to in Article </span><span>26</span><span>, content originating in third countries with which the Union has concluded an agreement establishing a free trade area or a customs union shall be deemed to be of Union origin</span><span>.</span><span> </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>4.</span></span><span>The Commission </span><span>shall </span><span>adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article </span><span>44</span><span> to exclude, in whole or in part, a third country from the scope of paragraph 1 based on any of the following criteria: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(h)</span></span><span>that third country has failed to provide national treatment related to Union products or entities under the agreements referred to in paragraph 1 </span><span>in relation to any of the net-zero technologies listed in Article 4, point (1);</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(i)</span></span><span>such exclusion is justified to avoid dependencies or any other developments that may threaten the security of supply in the Union of the products in question;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(j)</span></span><span>such exclusion</span><span> is justified under any other exception under the applicable agreement.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle"/>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28g</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Content equivalent to Union origin in other forms of public intervention</span>
            </p>
            <p class="NumPar11">
               <span>1.</span><span> </span><span>
                  <span class="tab">   </span></span><span>With respect the Union origin requirements set out in Article </span><span>28a</span><span>, content originating in third countries with which the Union has concluded an agreement establishing a free trade area or a customs union shall be deemed to be of Union origin</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2. </span></span><span>The </span><span>Commission</span><span> </span><span>shall </span><span>adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article </span><span>44</span><span> to exclude, in whole or in part, a third country from the scope of paragraph 1 based on any of the following criteria: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(k)</span></span><span>that third country has failed to provide national treatment related to Union products or entities under the agreements referred to in paragraph 1 in relation to any of the net-zero technologies listed in Article 4, point (1);</span>
            </p>
         </div>
         <div class="content">
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(l)</span></span><span>such exclusion is justified to avoid dependencies or any other developments that may threaten the security of supply in the Union of the products in question;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(m)</span></span><span>such exclusion is justified under any other exception under the applicable agreement.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="Titrearticle">
               <span>Article 28</span><span>h</span>
               <br/>
               <span>Delegation of power</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The Commission </span><span>is empowered</span><span> </span><span>to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 44 to </span><span>amend</span><span> </span><span>the Union origin requirements laid down in Annex II, taking into account the following criteria:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the market situation at Union level including declining Union market shares and Union industry producing below capacity;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the contribution of the requirements to the Union’s objective of public order, economic security, resilience and climate neutrality set out in Regulation (EU) 2021/1119;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>technological progress;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>demand for the relevant net-zero technologies; </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(e)</span></span><span>the impact of setting Union origin requirements on the overall competitiveness and greenhouse gas emissions of the relevant sectors.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>2.</span></span><span>The Commission</span><span> </span><span>is empowered to</span><span> adopt delegated acts to supplement Annex II with Union origin requirements for additional specific net-zero technology final products referred to in Article 4(1), points (g), (</span><span>h)</span><span>,</span><span> (j), (k), (n), (p), and (s), as well as </span><span>solar thermal technologies referred to in Article 4(1), point (a), </span><span>nuclear fuel cycle technologies referred to in Article 4(1), point (i), and electric propulsion technologies for transport referred to in Article 4(1), point (r), which shall be required in accordance with Articles 25</span><span>a</span><span>, 26, 28</span><span>a</span><span> and 28</span><span>c</span><span>. In doing so, the Commission shall take </span><span>the following </span><span>into account: </span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the market situation at Union level, as identified through monitoring activities, including declining Union market shares and Union industry producing below capacity;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the contribution of the requirements to the Union’s objective of public order, economic security, resilience and climate neutrality;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(c)</span></span><span>the impact of setting Union origin requirements, low-carbon requirements, or both on the overall competitiveness and greenhouse gas emissions of the relevant sectors</span><span>, </span><span>as well as on downstream costs for consumers and small and medium enterprises and on public budgets</span><span>.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(d)</span></span><span>demand for the relevant products or technologies.</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li ManualNumPar1">
               <span class="num"><span>1.</span></span><span>The delegated acts referred to in paragraph 2 shall set out:</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(a)</span></span><span>the products </span><span>and components </span><span>to which the minimum Union origin requirements shall apply;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point1">
               <span class="num"><span>(b)</span></span><span>the scope of application of the minimum Union origin requirements;</span>
            </p>
            <p class="li Point0">
